proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a balanced even-cactus diameter formula, a budget design algorithm, and a compact cactus LP for nonuniform singleton margins, then verified the cited cycle cut-polytope source. D0.5 graded the package incremental below the fixed field floor and found two unresolved soundness defects in the endpoint construction and baseline-menu definition. This archive is a research record, not a sound reusable theorem package; literature positioning also remains unresolved.
tldr: A data steward chooses priced noisy target cross-tabulations before reporting a transported trial effect. Conditional on a valid simultaneous cellwise CATE band, exact balanced singleton target shares, a signed interaction graph whose negative edges form a cut on the nonzero coefficient support, and an even-cactus pair-release graph, the correct loss compares two target-law completions and two CATE completions that can generate one common report. In that balanced regime, arbitrary fitted singleton CATE coefficients cancel and the remaining pair-coordinate loss has an explicit cycle-corrected formula, attainable endpoints, an exact budget dynamic program, and a gain-relative FPTAS. For nonuniform or noisy singleton margins, an exact compact junction-tree LP now computes the sharp paired diameter on any cactus, including odd cycles, without restricting target dependence. A fully specified synthetic workflow shows that a release with zero fitted pair coefficient changes the sharp interval from \([-0.16,0.48]\) to \([0.01,0.47]\).
gap: Aggregate-margin partial identification, signed cycle-polytope compatibility, query design, and budgeted causal data collection are established separately, but they do not give the honest precision frontier for priced overlapping pair-table releases under joint trial and target uncertainty.
fill: The project derives the paired-completion reduction, proves singleton-term cancellation after a valid signed-graph switch, obtains the sharp cactus formula and endpoints, constructs the exact budget recursion and gain-relative FPTAS, and poses nonuniform or approximate singleton balance as the named open extension.
